hero.headline: Record Fourth of July travel brings heavy traffic and rain to South Florida roads
hero.teaser: AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans traveled at least 50 miles from home this holiday weekend, with 61.4 million making the trip by car, creating heavy traffic on the Florida Turnpike and other South Florida roads.
hero.body:
A record-breaking number of Americans are hitting the roads this Fourth of July weekend, creating significant congestion across South Florida. According to AAA, 72.2 million people are expected to travel at least 50 miles from home between June 27 and July 5, with 61.4 million of those trips made by car. The combination of this unprecedented travel volume and Friday's heavy rainfall has made conditions particularly challenging on major highways like the Florida Turnpike south of Orlando. The wet weather has complicated driving conditions, with one driver commenting that "it starts raining and then everyone forgets how to drive."

Orlando and Miami have emerged as top-five travel destinations for this Independence Day holiday. Despite the crowded roads and adverse weather, many drivers continued with their plans. Some, like Carlos Borras and his wife who completed a round trip between Orlando and Miami on Friday, had surprisingly positive experiences. Borras reported that he "didn't see any traffic, no accidents or anything, so it's been great." However, not all drivers shared this experience. Fernando Amado described busy conditions worsened by the weather, noting that more people seemed to be hitting the road on Friday than he expected.

The timing of travel significantly impacts the driving experience, and AAA has identified specific windows when roads are less congested. The organization recommends that drivers still planning to travel should depart after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday to minimize time spent in traffic. The worst congestion is projected between 10 a.m. and noon on Saturday and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday. Where travelers are coming from, their destination, and departure time all play crucial roles in determining how smooth their journey will be.

As Americans navigate this record holiday travel period, the sheer scale of movement on the roads is striking. One driver acknowledged the enormity of the situation, expressing surprise that people could manage to afford all the gas needed for such widespread travel. Those who must travel during peak hours should prepare for delays and exercise extra caution, particularly during wet weather conditions. The combination of record-breaking travel numbers and unpredictable weather means South Florida roads will remain congested throughout the holiday weekend.

cards.headline: Supreme Court rules states may count absentee ballots received after Election Day
cards.teaser: The Supreme Court ruled 5-4 that states may count absentee ballots postmarked by Election Day but received afterward, providing clarity to Florida and other states with grace period laws.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court handed election administrators across the country significant clarity Monday, ruling 5-4 that states may count absentee ballots postmarked by Election Day but received afterward, preserving grace period laws that election officials in several states depend on to process ballots. The case, Republican National Committee v. Mississippi, centered on a Mississippi law allowing ballots received up to five business days after Election Day to count, provided they bear an Election Day postmark. A panel of three Trump-appointed Fifth Circuit judges had struck the law down in 2024, reading federal election statutes to require ballots to be received, not merely cast, by Election Day.

The Supreme Court reversed that ruling. Justice Amy Coney Barrett, herself a Trump appointee, wrote the majority opinion and was joined by Chief Justice Roberts and the three liberal justices. Barrett wrote that federal law establishes when voters must make their choice, not when officials must have their ballots in hand. The election-day statutes say nothing about ballot receipt, she wrote, and we cannot add to the words Congress chose. The decision affects election procedures in Florida and other states with similar grace period provisions for absentee ballots.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to win 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach is celebrating after being named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, the only Florida city selected this year.
cards.body:
Riviera Beach is celebrating after being named one of only 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League. The city was the only Florida community selected for the honor this year. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented the city's efforts to strengthen community engagement. Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment for the city, saying "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." He said the city earned the award through a long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents, noting that people are seeing the changes and reimagining of the city that leaders set out to accomplish years ago.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted several civic engagement programs including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership, the Citizens Leadership Academy with a 98 percent completion rate, and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to longtime homeowners for critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson said the award is a tribute to the heart and determination of residents, adding that winning brings back community pride. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.

cards.headline: Argentina survives Cape Verde 3-2 in extra time to advance to World Cup Round of 16
cards.teaser: Lionel Messi and defending World Cup champion Argentina beat Cape Verde 3-2 on Friday in a thrilling match that went to extra time in South Florida.
cards.body:
Argentina advanced to the World Cup Round of 16 after defeating Cape Verde 3-2 in extra time on Friday before a pro-Argentina crowd in South Florida. The go-ahead score was credited as an own-goal after Cristian Romero's header deflected off Cape Verde's Diney Borges in the 111th minute. Lisandro Martinez scored in the 103rd minute to put Argentina ahead 2-1.

Lionel Messi scored his record-extending 20th career World Cup goal in the 29th minute, sneaking behind the Cape Verde defense on a well-timed run as Martinez lofted a pass toward him. Messi took a quick touch and hammered a finish into the roof of the net past goalkeeper Vozinha for a 1-0 lead. Sidny Lopes Cabral and Deroy Duarte scored equalizers for Cape Verde that stunned the crowd.

Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha, who is 40 years old, had 10 saves against Argentina, including five against Messi. Argentina will face Egypt in Atlanta on Tuesday after Egypt beat Australia in a penalty shootout earlier Friday. Messi has seven goals in this tournament, one more than France's Kylian Mbappé in the Golden Boot race, and has 12 goals during his record eight-match scoring streak.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Let Late Lead Slip Away in 10-3 Loss to Tarpons
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie Mets were six outs away from ending their losing streak Saturday before a disastrous eighth inning turned a 3-1 lead into a 10-3 loss to the Tampa Tarpons at Clover P
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets were six outs away from ending their losing streak Saturday before a disastrous eighth inning turned a 3-1 lead into a 10-3 loss to the Tampa Tarpons at Clover Park.

Tampa scored six unearned runs in the eighth inning, capitalizing on four Mets errors, then added three more runs in the ninth to pull away on Independence Day. The Tarpons extended their winning streak to eight games, while St. Lucie dropped its ninth straight.

The Mets led 3-1 entering the eighth after building the advantage with timely offense and strong relief work. But Tampa's comeback began after Hans Montero reached and eventually scored the tying run when Bryce Martin-Grudzielanek hit a two-out ground ball to third baseman Branny De Oleo. The ball deflected off De Oleo's glove for an error, allowing Montero to come home and even the game at 3-3.

The inning continued from there, and David McCann delivered the decisive blow with a three-run home run off Conner Ware to give Tampa a 6-3 lead. McCann struck again in the ninth, launching another three-run homer off Luis Alvarez to make it 10-3.

McCann finished 3-for-4 with two home runs, a single, a walk and seven RBI. The performance came one day after he went 0-for-4 with four strikeouts.

St. Lucie had trailed 1-0 early before tying the game in the fourth inning on an RBI groundout by Simon Juan. Chase Meggers gave the Mets a 2-1 lead in the fifth with a two-out RBI single against Tyler Boudreau. Juan then added a solo home run off Boudreau in the sixth to stretch the lead to 3-1.

Ware had kept Tampa quiet through three scoreless innings before the eighth-inning unraveling. He took the loss after allowing five runs over 3.2 innings, though all five were unearned.

Tampa reliever Jose M. Rodriguez earned the win after pitching a perfect seventh inning.

The Mets fell to 2-10 in the second half and 35-43 overall. Tampa improved to 11-3 in the second half and 46-34 overall.

The teams close their six-game series Sunday at Clover Park, with first pitch scheduled for 12:10 p.m. It will be Little League Day. Little leaguers who wear their jerseys will receive free admission and a gift courtesy of Holiday Inn Express.

cards.headline: U.S. men's soccer team faces Belgium Monday after controversial red card
cards.teaser: The United States men's national team takes the field Monday night against Belgium in the World Cup Round of 16 after earning their first knockout stage victory since 2002.
cards.body:
The United States men's national team takes the field Monday night against Belgium in the Round of 16 at Lumen Field in Seattle. The Americans earned the program's first knockout stage victory since 2002, having dispatched Bosnia and Herzegovina 2-0 on Wednesday night while playing the final 36 minutes with 10 men after Folarin Balogun was red-carded on a maddening call. Longtime Premier League VAR referee Andy Davies called the decision wrong, telling ESPN the contact was purely accidental and an unfortunate result from two players challenging for possession of the ball in a normal football movement. Coach Mauricio Pochettino said flatly it was never a red card and pointed out that Lionel Messi made a nearly identical challenge against Algeria earlier in the tournament and received nothing.

Weston McKennie spoke for the locker room, saying he thinks it's a bit bogus. Balogun, one of their top players, will watch Monday from the bench against a Belgian side that earned a Round of 16 win over the United States in the 2014 World Cup. Belgium has won six consecutive meetings against the U.S. since the inaugural 1930 World Cup, the lone American victory in the head-to-head. The Americans won Wednesday without Balogun for the better part of an hour and will play at a venue where the home crowd will be as loud as any in the tournament.

cards.headline: Juno Beach residents push for fence replacement at JB-7 beach access as town weighs budget impact
cards.teaser: A missing fence at the JB-7 public beach access point is causing conflict between Colony Condos residents and beachgoers, with a replacement potentially costing the town thousands of dollars.
cards.body:
Residents at the Colony Condos say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons. Without it, only bushes separate the public access path from private land. Lori Hill, a Colony resident, said the problem peaks in summer. "Lots of cars that just come at random, and then they just park on the spots there," Hill said. "Bushes are pushed back that they cut through those with their coolers and their fishing rods and lawn chairs and everything, and then they just park there all day." Hill said residents have had confrontations with trespassers and now call the police to address the issue.

Not everyone on the beach sees a major problem. Beachgoer Michael House said he walks to JB-7 from a public lot a couple of blocks away and has not witnessed the issues residents describe. The dispute came before the Juno Beach Town Council at a recent meeting, where a town official noted the town is not obligated to install a fence. Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern suggested exploring lower-cost solutions. "I understand fencing is expensive, but I'd like to see maybe we can help them with a lower-cost fence or some combination of split rail and shrubs," Halpern said. The council agreed to address the fence question during budget discussions on July 15.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: The City of Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, marking the only Florida city selected this year.
cards.body:
Riviera Beach has been named one of 10 U.S. communities to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented the city's efforts to strengthen community engagement. Mayor Douglas Lawson said the recognition reflects years of work focused on improving civic health and strengthening trust between residents and local government. "They're seeing the changes; they're seeing the revitalization and the reimagining of Riviera Beach that we set out so many years to do," Lawson said.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted several programs designed to increase civic participation and neighborhood investment. These include the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy; the Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education initiative with a 98 percent completion rate; and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, saying the award reinforces the city's positive momentum and brings back community pride. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive 'A' rating from state with record graduation rate
cards.teaser: The School District of Palm Beach County received an 'A' rating from the state for the third year in a row, with 143 district-operated schools rated A or B and a record-setting 93.5% graduation rate.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County earned an "A" rating from the state for the third consecutive year, with 143 district-operated schools, or 84%, rated "A" or "B" this year, up from 120 schools the previous year. The district achieved a record-setting 93.5% graduation rate. District leaders reported that 86% of seniors participated in college-level coursework, taking at least one Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment course. Additionally, 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma.

One of the district's biggest successes came from S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach, which dramatically improved from a "C" rating last year to an "A" this year. Principal Rona Tata, who has served 15 years as principal and five years as assistant principal, attributed the turnaround to modifying the school's early childhood curriculum program, which serves students starting at age 3 through kindergarten. The school was one of four district schools to improve from a "C" to an "A" rating this year. The others were Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk Facebook post
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year following controversial social media .
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk. Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, sparked controversy with his comments, which labeled Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in recommending Theobald get his job back, saying "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney claims Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a "serious offense" and removing him was appropriate.

In an order issued last month, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge also recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report obtained by WPTV, Theobald admitted writing the comments about Kirk but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4% this year, ground beef and strawberries hit hardest
cards.teaser: A Fourth of July meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
cards.body:
According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. The survey points squarely at inflation, with ground beef up 5.5% and buns up 7.7%. Strawberries, hit hard by a Florida frost, are up 12.4%. Ice cream prices have also increased by 5.3%.

Not everything is more expensive, though. Potato prices are down this year, which is good news for potato chip and salad lovers. Corn prices have fluctuated, but locally grown corn from the Glades can offer the best deal. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch said there are ways to keep costs in check. "It's really important to shop savvier than ever, it is comparing the stores to see who has the best deals for the groceries on your list, the biggest thing for families is cutting down the food waste, and that begins with a meal plan," Woroch said.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie expands Midway Road, adds Florida Turnpike interchange
hero.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved giving 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike at Midway Road as part of a $95 million widening project.
hero.body:
Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a new Turnpike interchange. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie. The interchange is designed to accommodate growth that has already occurred and growth expected over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT is constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to address congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also working on improving the Turnpike bridge and adding a partial interchange, both still in the design phase. The project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Glydways proposes elevated self-driving transit connecting West Palm Beach to airport
cards.teaser: A California-based company will present a proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for an elevated network of autonomous vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport.
cards.body:
Glydways will present the proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for initial consideration. The system would connect the airport, convention center, Brightline and Tri-Rail stations using small autonomous electric vehicles carrying four to six passengers on an elevated guideway above existing roads. The company estimates travel times of seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center.

Glydways Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said the system would cost a small fraction of traditional light rail, which has carried estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile in previous South Florida discussions. Funding could come from Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. Gettinger said the service would be priced more like public transit than a private rideshare, emphasizing this is not a $30 ride between downtown and the airport.

Travelers outside the airport described long waits and expensive rideshare trips. Christy Selman said she recently waited more than 25 minutes for a rideshare and paid about $40 for the trip. Tuesday's County Commission meeting is not expected to approve construction but rather determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal.

cards.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation transforms Fort Pierce into artistic destination
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation in Fort Pierce is transforming the city into an artistic destination, preserving the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain who once lived in the historic Crain Estate and offering tours and artist residencies.
cards.body:
Rewritten Card Body

Tucked away in the historic Crain Estate, the Peacock House Art Foundation preserves the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain, who once called the property home. Mr. Crain was a tile worker by trade, and his craftsmanship is visible throughout the facility, from the ground to the walls to the ceiling. The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items for their Florida estate, including a gazebo shipped from India. Many parts of the house remain unchanged from when the Crains lived there, including the smoking and bourbon room. The foundation has preserved 90 percent of the estate in its original state. The Peacock House gets its name from the birds that have roamed the property for decades. The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, bringing in seven originally, which has grown to over 100. Among them is a beloved bird named Bob, believed to be 60 years old and identified by his distinctive limp.

Visitors can take guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts artists from around the world, offering simple but elegant accommodations on the property. The art lab offers classes for children and adults of all skill levels, with art director Krystal Masters leading one-on-one classes designed for complete beginners. Classes cover mediums including sculpting and watercolor. According to Masters, art functions as therapy and helps people destress, with the goal of helping students walk away fulfilled.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County marine deputies rescue 2 after boat sinks in Intracoastal Waterway
cards.teaser: Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on Wednesday, saved by marine deputies and the life-saving decision to wear life jackets.
cards.body:
Two boaters are safe after their vessel sank in the Intracoastal Waterway on July 1, thanks to a quick response from St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office Marine Unit deputies and the life-saving decision to wear life jackets. Both occupants ended up in the water when their small motorized boat took on water and became submerged. Body-worn camera footage captured the rescue as it unfolded.

Marine Unit deputies quickly located the pair in the water and safely brought them aboard their patrol vessel. The boaters were then transported back to the boat ramp without any injuries reported. "This incident serves as an important reminder that wearing a life jacket can save your life," the sheriff's office said in a Facebook post. "We're grateful this call ended safely and proud of the swift response by our Marine Unit deputies who are always ready to answer the call."

cards.headline: Stuart's downtown dock closes Monday for $3 million renovation, doubling boat slip capacity
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The year-long project will nearly double the facility's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock, and a smaller floating platform. The project is funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees. With more than 1,400 boaters using the dock annually, Stuart Mayor Sean Reed emphasized that the upgrades serve a critical safety function. "They're doing it to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms," Reed said. "So the year of waiting will be worth it."

During the closure, the city is accommodating businesses that depend on the dock. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates from the facility, initially had concerns about continuing operations. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the city found a solution by allowing the company to build a gate at the non-floating section of the dock for boarding passengers. Kuyrkendall acknowledged current limitations, noting that crowded weekends create challenges. "On the weekend that's when it can get a little hectic at the dock and you know it's never great for us when we're squeezing in and trying to find spots," he said. He stressed the dock's importance to Stuart's identity and economy, calling the modernization project beneficial for both the city and local businesses.

hero.headline: Serena Williams withdraws from Wimbledon doubles with sister Venus due to knee injury
hero.teaser: Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday due to a right knee injury sustained during her singles return earlier in the week.
hero.body:
Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday due to a right knee injury sustained during her singles return earlier in the week. The 44-year-old lost to 20-year-old Maya Joint of Australia 6-3, 6-7 (6), 6-3 on Tuesday. "I'm heartbroken to have to withdraw from doubles. Coming back to compete again has been a gift, and the opportunity to play alongside Venus once more meant the world to me. I did everything I could but unfortunately my knee just isn't ready to compete," Serena said in an Instagram post.

The post included images of four syringes showing fluid drained from her knee after her singles match, along with a video of her walking with strapping on her right leg and what appeared to be one of her daughters holding a cane for her. The Williams sisters were scheduled to play Camila Osorio and Solana Sierra in the only first-round doubles match not scheduled earlier in the week, which had been pushed back to allow Serena more recovery time. Venus, 46, played in the mixed doubles tournament Friday with Kevin Krawietz, losing in straight sets to Tereza Mihalikova and Lloyd Glasspool. The pair are six-time Wimbledon women's doubles champions. With the U.S. Open approaching, Serena hinted at future competition, saying "stay tuned to a city near you."

cards.teaser: Lionel Messi and defending World Cup champion Argentina beat Cape Verde 3-2 on Friday in a thrilling match that went to extra time in South Florida.
cards.body:
Argentina advanced to the World Cup Round of 16 after defeating Cape Verde 3-2 in extra time on Friday before a pro-Argentina crowd in South Florida. The go-ahead score was credited as an own-goal after Cristian Romero's header deflected off Cape Verde's Diney Borges in the 111th minute. Lisandro Martinez scored in the 103rd minute to put Argentina ahead 2-1.

Lionel Messi scored his record-extending 20th career World Cup goal in the 29th minute, sneaking behind the Cape Verde defense on a well-timed run as Martinez lofted a pass toward him. Messi took a quick touch and hammered a finish into the roof of the net past goalkeeper Vozinha for a 1-0 lead. Sidny Lopes Cabral and Deroy Duarte scored equalizers for Cape Verde that stunned the crowd.

Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha, who is 40 years old, had 10 saves against Argentina, including five against Messi. Argentina will face Egypt in Atlanta on Tuesday after Egypt beat Australia in a penalty shootout earlier Friday. Messi has seven goals in this tournament, one more than France's Kylian Mbappé in the Golden Boot race, and has 12 goals during his record eight-match scoring streak.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season and district championship
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football program finished last season with a 10-2 record and a district title, but a second-round playoff exit has motivated the team to aim higher for the 2026 fall season. Head coach Jimmy Robertson highlighted the strength of the senior class, noting that most are four-year players who came through the middle school program. "Hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had," Robertson said. With this veteran leadership in place, the Scots are positioned to compete for a state title.

The program has deliberately scheduled tougher opponents this fall as part of their strategy to elevate performance. Senior Jack Williams explained the reasoning behind the challenging schedule: "We really have a challenging schedule for this year because we wanna compete and take that next level, and it's by playing against really good teams that we do that and attract new people." For the Scots, success is specifically measured by advancing further in the postseason. Senior Jack Whelche stated that while an undefeated regular season is a goal, it becomes meaningless if the team continues losing in the second round. Senior Edmyer St. Jean emphasized that summer workouts serve as daily motivation for the team's push toward results when the season begins.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Let Late Lead Slip Away in 10-3 Loss to Tarpons
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie Mets were six outs away from ending their losing streak Saturday before a disastrous eighth inning turned a 3-1 lead into a 10-3 loss to the Tampa Tarpons at Clover P
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets were six outs away from ending their losing streak Saturday before a disastrous eighth inning turned a 3-1 lead into a 10-3 loss to the Tampa Tarpons at Clover Park.

Tampa scored six unearned runs in the eighth inning, capitalizing on four Mets errors, then added three more runs in the ninth to pull away on Independence Day. The Tarpons extended their winning streak to eight games, while St. Lucie dropped its ninth straight.

The Mets led 3-1 entering the eighth after building the advantage with timely offense and strong relief work. But Tampa's comeback began after Hans Montero reached and eventually scored the tying run when Bryce Martin-Grudzielanek hit a two-out ground ball to third baseman Branny De Oleo. The ball deflected off De Oleo's glove for an error, allowing Montero to come home and even the game at 3-3.

The inning continued from there, and David McCann delivered the decisive blow with a three-run home run off Conner Ware to give Tampa a 6-3 lead. McCann struck again in the ninth, launching another three-run homer off Luis Alvarez to make it 10-3.

McCann finished 3-for-4 with two home runs, a single, a walk and seven RBI. The performance came one day after he went 0-for-4 with four strikeouts.

St. Lucie had trailed 1-0 early before tying the game in the fourth inning on an RBI groundout by Simon Juan. Chase Meggers gave the Mets a 2-1 lead in the fifth with a two-out RBI single against Tyler Boudreau. Juan then added a solo home run off Boudreau in the sixth to stretch the lead to 3-1.

Ware had kept Tampa quiet through three scoreless innings before the eighth-inning unraveling. He took the loss after allowing five runs over 3.2 innings, though all five were unearned.

Tampa reliever Jose M. Rodriguez earned the win after pitching a perfect seventh inning.

The Mets fell to 2-10 in the second half and 35-43 overall. Tampa improved to 11-3 in the second half and 46-34 overall.

The teams close their six-game series Sunday at Clover Park, with first pitch scheduled for 12:10 p.m. It will be Little League Day. Little leaguers who wear their jerseys will receive free admission and a gift courtesy of Holiday Inn Express.

hero.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach offers sea turtle nesting programs through September
hero.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs during peak sea turtle nesting season through September. Guests can participate in guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. The programs are designed to give visitors an opportunity to learn more about sea turtle conservation along one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The center's Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations during the programs may include the use of red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment. The center's education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Conservation groups continue encouraging beachgoers to turn off beachfront lighting at night, properly dispose of trash and avoid disturbing nesting turtles or hatchlings. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

cards.headline: North Palm Beach hosts Fourth of July fireworks and pool party at country club
cards.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors celebrated Independence Day with family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club on July 4.
cards.body:
The free community event included a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m. Organizers said this years event also recognized Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County.

The festivities began with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests enjoyed a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families took part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign began around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course offered one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse also hosted a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

hero.headline: U.S. men's soccer team faces Belgium Monday after controversial red card
hero.teaser: The United States men's national team takes the field Monday night against Belgium in the World Cup Round of 16 after earning their first knockout stage victory since 2002.
hero.body:
The United States men's national team takes the field Monday night against Belgium in the Round of 16 at Lumen Field in Seattle. The Americans earned the program's first knockout stage victory since 2002, having dispatched Bosnia and Herzegovina 2-0 on Wednesday night while playing the final 36 minutes with 10 men after Folarin Balogun was red-carded on a maddening call. Longtime Premier League VAR referee Andy Davies called the decision wrong, telling ESPN the contact was purely accidental and an unfortunate result from two players challenging for possession of the ball in a normal football movement. Coach Mauricio Pochettino said flatly it was never a red card and pointed out that Lionel Messi made a nearly identical challenge against Algeria earlier in the tournament and received nothing.

Weston McKennie spoke for the locker room, saying he thinks it's a bit bogus. Balogun, one of their top players, will watch Monday from the bench against a Belgian side that earned a Round of 16 win over the United States in the 2014 World Cup. Belgium has won six consecutive meetings against the U.S. since the inaugural 1930 World Cup, the lone American victory in the head-to-head. The Americans won Wednesday without Balogun for the better part of an hour and will play at a venue where the home crowd will be as loud as any in the tournament.

cards.headline: Supreme Court rules states may count absentee ballots received after Election Day
cards.teaser: The Supreme Court ruled 5-4 that states may count absentee ballots postmarked by Election Day but received afterward, providing clarity to Florida and other states with grace period laws.
cards.body:
The Supreme Court handed election administrators across the country significant clarity Monday, ruling 5-4 that states may count absentee ballots postmarked by Election Day but received afterward, preserving grace period laws that election officials in several states depend on to process ballots. The case, Republican National Committee v. Mississippi, centered on a Mississippi law allowing ballots received up to five business days after Election Day to count, provided they bear an Election Day postmark. A panel of three Trump-appointed Fifth Circuit judges had struck the law down in 2024, reading federal election statutes to require ballots to be received, not merely cast, by Election Day.

The Supreme Court reversed that ruling. Justice Amy Coney Barrett, herself a Trump appointee, wrote the majority opinion and was joined by Chief Justice Roberts and the three liberal justices. Barrett wrote that federal law establishes when voters must make their choice, not when officials must have their ballots in hand. The election-day statutes say nothing about ballot receipt, she wrote, and we cannot add to the words Congress chose. The decision affects election procedures in Florida and other states with similar grace period provisions for absentee ballots.

hero.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation transforms Fort Pierce historic estate into arts destination
hero.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation has established itself as a cultural hub in Fort Pierce, revitalizing the historic Crain Estate and creating a space where local and international artists converge. The nonprofit organization preserves the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain, the original owners who filled their home with treasures collected during nine trips around the world. Krystal Masters, the art director, leads guided tours of the property's lush gardens and distinctive architecture every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, showcasing how the estate remains approximately 90 percent unchanged from the Crains' era. The craftsmanship of Jaxson Crain, a tile worker by trade, is evident throughout the facility, visible on floors, walls, and ceilings. Among the estate's preserved spaces is the smoking and bourbon room, featuring dark wood paneling, masculine color schemes, and decorative stained glass that opens onto a front patio bar. The couple's worldly acquisitions include a gazebo shipped from India, complete with peacock designs carved into its structure.

The peacocks themselves are central to the property's identity and history. The Crains are believed to have introduced the birds to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, starting with seven birds that have multiplied to over 100. Bob, a 60-year-old peacock who walks with a limp, has become something of a celebrity at the estate, receiving daily hand feedings from his own set of bowls. Visitors, particularly children, find memorable moments interacting with the peacocks during tours. The property once housed monkeys as well, with one account describing how Jackson Crain traveled to South America and returned home with a baby monkey tucked in his pocket.

The foundation operates an artist-in-residency program that attracts creative professionals from around the world, offering simple yet elegant accommodations on the property. Masters emphasizes that the foundation has deliberately avoided commercializing the estate while maintaining its original character. The art lab provides classes for children and adults of all skill levels, with most instruction delivered through one-on-one sessions. Beginners arrive with no experience and leave with completed artwork. Masters teaches various mediums including sculpting and watercolor, with workshops like "Paint Your Pet in Watercolor and Rainbow" drawing participants seeking creative outlets.

For Masters, art serves a therapeutic purpose beyond simple creativity. She describes it as a form of stress relief that allows people to disconnect from their devices and leave feeling fulfilled. The foundation's commitment to accessibility means anyone can participate in workshops featuring different artistic techniques and projects. This approach has created a welcoming environment where the historic estate functions as both a cultural destination and a healing space for the community.
